policy.purpose: Add traceable authentic reading to existing English instruction without creating parallel grades, mastery, or learner records.
policy.offlineRule: The existing first-party unit text remains available offline; authentic-source links must be printable/downloadable and should be locally archived in a later source-packet pass.

english-9.title: The Story of an Hour
english-9.author: Kate Chopin
english-9.publicDomainBasis: Public domain in the United States
english-9.focus: observation versus inference; diction; reversal; evidence limits
english-9.evidenceTask: Annotate three details whose meaning changes after the ending. Write a claim, identify one competing interpretation, and revise the claim after rereading.

english-9.title: Gettysburg Address
english-9.author: Abraham Lincoln
english-9.provenance: Speech delivered at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, November 19, 1863
english-9.publicDomainBasis: Public domain historical text published in the United States
english-9.focus: purpose; repetition; compression; claim and evidence
english-9.evidenceTask: Trace how repeated words develop Lincoln's claim. Distinguish what the speech asserts from historical information it assumes.

english-9.title: The Open Window
english-9.author: Saki (H. H. Munro)
english-9.publicDomainBasis: Published before 1931; public domain in the United States
english-9.focus: narrative reliability; inference; revision; academic integrity
english-9.evidenceTask: Build two interpretations of Vera's story, identify the textual evidence available at each stage, then explain why a responsible reader revises rather than hides an earlier inference.

english-10.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
english-10.author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
english-10.provenance: First published in The New England Magazine, 1892
english-10.publicDomainBasis: Public domain in the United States
english-10.focus: perspective; narrator reliability; social context; interpretive qualification
english-10.evidenceTask: Track three places where the narrator's description and the reader's inference diverge. Qualify a claim so it does not diagnose the narrator or exceed the text.

english-10.title: Women's Rights Convention report of Sojourner Truth's speech
english-10.author: Sojourner Truth; reported by Marius Robinson
english-10.provenance: Anti-Slavery Bugle report by Marius Robinson, the earliest full report
english-10.publicDomainBasis: Published in the United States in 1851; public domain
english-10.evidenceTask: Separate Truth's reported argument from the reporter's framing. Record what can be claimed confidently from this version and what requires version comparison.

english-10.title: Declaration of Sentiments
english-10.author: Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Seneca Falls Convention participants
english-10.evidenceTask: Paraphrase one grievance without flattening its meaning, compare its structure with the Declaration of Independence, and document exactly where the parallel ends.

english-11.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, Chapter VII
english-11.author: Frederick Douglass
english-11.provenance: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave, 1845
english-11.focus: literacy; rhetoric; autobiographical evidence; historical context
english-11.evidenceTask: Analyze how Douglass turns literacy into both narrative event and argument. Distinguish remembered experience, quoted dialogue, and later authorial interpretation.

english-11.title: The Souls of Black Folk, Chapter I: Of Our Spiritual Strivings
english-11.author: W. E. B. Du Bois
english-11.provenance: The Souls of Black Folk, first published 1903
english-11.publicDomainBasis: Published before 1931; public domain in the United States
english-11.focus: concept formation; metaphor; historical argument; scholarly qualification
english-11.evidenceTask: Define one key concept using Du Bois's own development of it, then test whether a modern paraphrase preserves the concept's historical and rhetorical complexity.

english-11.title: Self-Reliance
english-11.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
english-11.assignedSpan: Opening through the discussion of consistency; teacher may assign the complete essay
english-11.evidenceTask: Select two claims that appear to conflict. Explain the tension through syntax and context, then revise a simplistic summary into a defensible thesis.

english-12.title: A Modest Proposal
english-12.author: Jonathan Swift
english-12.focus: satire; persona; quantitative rhetoric; ethical interpretation
english-12.evidenceTask: Separate Swift's literal persona from the essay's satirical target. Audit one numerical claim for rhetorical function and explain what evidence would be needed to treat it as empirical rather than satirical.

english-12.title: On Liberty, Chapter II: Of the Liberty of Thought and Discussion
english-12.author: John Stuart Mill
english-12.assignedSpan: Chapter II, with teacher-selected passages for close reading
english-12.provenance: On Liberty, first published 1859; public domain fourth edition also available
english-12.evidenceTask: Map Mill's argument as claims, concessions, and consequences. Identify one assumption that must hold for the argument to work and one plausible challenge.

english-12.title: A Room of One's Own
english-12.author: Virginia Woolf
english-12.assignedSpan: Chapter I; optional continuation into Chapter III for advanced pathway
english-12.publicDomainBasis: Published in 1929; entered the U.S. public domain January 1, 2025
english-12.focus: method; evidence limits; narrative essay voice; authorship and intellectual independence
english-12.evidenceTask: Track how Woolf moves between scene, hypothetical reasoning, evidence, and qualification. Write a method note explaining which parts are observation, inference, example, or argument.
